raw_text:
Client overview
- 42-year-old male, desk worker.
- Prior L4–L5 disc herniation 8 months ago; currently asymptomatic.
- Physiotherapist restrictions: no heavy spinal loading and no loaded spinal flexion.
- Goal: general strength, safe progression, posture and core control, resilience for desk work.
- Equipment available: full gym.

Principles and precautions
- Avoid heavy axial loading (no heavy barbell back squats, heavy deadlifts, heavy barbell loaded flexion) and avoid loaded spinal flexion (no bent-over loaded flexion with spine rounding under load).
- Emphasize neutral spine, diaphragmatic breathing, hip hinge with pelvic control, and progressive loading mostly via unilateral work, machines, goblet variations, and horizontal pressing/rows.
- Start conservative and progress volume/intensity gradually. Monitor any recurrence of symptoms; if pain, stop that exercise and refer back to physio/GP.
- Include mobility (thoracic extension, hip extension, hamstrings) and posture-focused work for desk-related stiffness.
- Include targeted core control and anti-flexion/anti-rotation training rather than sit-up style loaded flexion.

Program structure (12 weeks)
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions per week, full-body emphasis each session to build general strength and resilience while allowing recovery for desk worker.
- Phases:
  - Phase A — Weeks 1–4: Foundation, motor control, movement patterning, low-moderate load.
  - Phase B — Weeks 5–8: Strength development, increased load and complexity while respecting spine rules.
  - Phase C — Weeks 9–12: Consolidation and higher intensity/volume within safety constraints; more unilateral and dynamic loading, conditioning.

Progression guidance
- Intensity: Use RPE approach. Weeks 1–4 work mostly RPE 5–7; Weeks 5–8 RPE 6–8; Weeks 9–12 RPE 7–8 (no maximal singles with heavy axial compressive load).
- Increase load by ~2.5–5% when target reps are achieved easily; otherwise increase sets or reduce rest time moderately.
- Emphasize quality over load: neutral spine, hinge from hips, avoid loaded flexion and any pain-provoking movements.
- Warm-up before sessions: 6–10 min light cardio + dynamic mobility + 2 warm-up sets of first compound exercise.

Session template (approx. 60–75 minutes)
- Warm-up (10–12 min)
- Strength compound/main movement (20–25 min)
- Secondary strength/unilateral + posterior chain (15–20 min)
- Core/anti-movement + mobility (10–15 min)
- Optional short conditioning finisher (5–10 min) if tolerated

Detailed 12-week plan

Phase A — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Focus: movement quality, core control, posterior chain activation, moderate loads.

Weeks 1–2 (3 sessions/week — A, B, C)
Session A
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min bike or row + thoracic rotations, hip CARs, glute bridges x10
2. Goblet squat: 3 sets x 8–10 reps (moderate load; keep chest up, neutral spine)
3. Romanian deadlift — dumbbell or light trap bar: 3 x 8 (soft knees, hip hinge; avoid heavy barbell straight bar if it causes compression)
4. Seated cable row (chest supported if available): 3 x 10
5. Split squat (rear-foot elevated or static lunge) dumbbells: 3 x 8 each leg
6. Pallof press (anti-rotation): 3 x 10 each side (slow, core braced)
7. Plank (front isometric) — 3 x 30–45 s (focus on breathing, neutral spine)
8. Thoracic extension mobilization: 2 x 10

Session B
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min elliptical + band pull-aparts, bird dogs
2. Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8–10
3. Single-leg Romanian deadlift (dumbbell): 3 x 8 each leg
4. Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 3 x 8–10
5. Kettlebell/DB hip thrust (bodyweight or light DB): 3 x 10–12
6. Farmer carry (light–moderate) 3 x 30–40 m — emphasis on upright posture (use two dumbbells)
7. Dead bug or dead-bug progressions: 3 x 10 each side
8. Hip flexor / hamstring mobility: 2–3 min each side

Session C
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min row + glute activation
2. Trap-bar deadlift (light–moderate) OR hex-bar Romanian variant focusing on lower load: 3 x 6–8 (keep neutral spine; stop if symptoms)
3. Chest-supported T-bar row or single-arm DB row: 3 x 8–10
4. Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 6–8 each leg
5. Seated overhead press (dumbbell) or machine: 3 x 8–10 (avoid heavy standing barbell overhead if it increases compression)
6. Side plank (knee or full): 3 x 20–40 s each side
7. Thoracic foam-roll + pec stretch: 2 x 45 s each

Weeks 3–4 — adjust reps/sets
- Slight progression: increase load or add 1 set to main lifts (e.g., goblet squat 4 x 8–10 or increase DB weight). Keep same exercises, focus on controlled eccentric and bracing.

Phase B — Strength Development (Weeks 5–8)
Focus: increase load, introduce more unilateral and machine variations for safety, more anti-rotation/core complexity.

Weeks 5–6
Session A
1. Warm-up (as before)
2. Barbell safety squat or Smith-machine box squat with light load OR heavy goblet to keep neutral spine: 4 x 6–8 (use box to limit depth if needed)
3. Romanian deadlift with dumbbells or trap bar: 4 x 6–8
4. Chest-supported row (3 x 8) + superset band pull-aparts (2 x 15)
5. Reverse lunge walking or stationary with DBs: 3 x 8 each leg
6. Pallof press with hold (3 x 8 + 3 x 6 s isometric holds)
7. Dead-bug with heavy emphasis on breathing + 60–90 s plank progression

Session B
1. Warm-up
2. Trap-bar deadlift moderate (3–4 x 5) — still moderate weight, not maximal (RPE ≤ 8)
3. Incline DB press: 4 x 6–8
4. Single-arm row 3 x 8 each side
5. Hip thrust (barbell but moderate load) 3 x 6–8 — keep pelvis control, avoid hyperextension at top
6. Farmer carry heavier (3 x 40–50 m) or suitcase carries for anti-lateral-flexion work
7. Pallof press variation (half-kneeling) 3 x 8 each side

Session C
1. Warm-up
2. Split-squat or rear-foot-elevated DB squat: 4 x 6–8 each leg
3. Seated leg press (controlled depth) 3 x 8–10 — good way to load legs without axial spine load
4. Seated overhead press machine or DB strict press seated (3 x 6–8)
5. Cable anti-rotation chops (controlled) 3 x 8 each side
6. Bird-dog progression with 3 x 8 each side holds
7. Hip mobility and thoracic extension work

Weeks 7–8 — progress
- Increase load by ~5% on compound moves if movement quality maintained. Add an extra set to primary lifts if recovery good (e.g., trap-bar 4 x 5). Introduce tempo work (3 s eccentric for one set) for control.

Phase C — Consolidation / Higher Intensity (Weeks 9–12)
Focus: higher intensity within safety limits, more complex core anti-flexion and functional carries, conditioning. Still avoid heavy axial compressive singles and loaded flexion.

Weeks 9–10
Session A
1. Warm-up
2. Goblet squat to box (or safety-bar squat if available and comfortable) 4 x 6 (heavier than prior, but maintain neutral spine)
3. Trap-bar deadlift or hex bar (moderate-heavy) 4 x 4–5 (stop short of maximal reps; RPE ≤ 8)
4. Chest-supported row or single-arm DB row 4 x 6–8
5. Walking lunges with DBs 3 x 12 steps total
6. Farmer carry heavy 4 x 40–50 m
7. Anti-extension roll-out progressions with wheel or cable (kneeling) 3 x 8 — only if client has good core control

Session B
1. Warm-up
2. Incline DB press heavier: 4 x 6
3. Single-leg Romanian deadlift with heavier DB: 4 x 6 each leg
4. Lat pulldown wide grip: 3 x 6–8
5. Glute bridge / barbell hip thrust 4 x 6–8
6. Suitcase carry 3 x 30 m each side
7. Side plank with leg raise 3 x 20–30 s each side

Session C
1. Warm-up
2. Bulgarian split squat heavier: 4 x 6 each leg
3. Seated leg press 4 x 8
4. Standing single-arm DB press (light–moderate) 3 x 8 each arm to train stability
5. Cable woodchop anti-rotation slow 3 x 8 each side
6. Bird-dog to loaded carry transition drills (carry + pause) 3 rounds
7. Mobility and breathing work

Weeks 11–12 — peak consolidation
- Maintain or slightly increase load if movement quality remains excellent. Consider small 1–2 week deload after Week 12.
- Sample tweaks: reduce reps to 4–6 on main lifts, increase carries distance, add cluster sets (e.g., 3 sets of 2+2 rest 20s) only for trap-bar deadlift if comfortable.

Conditioning (optional)
- 2 short conditioning sessions/week on non-lifting days or after lifts (10–20 min):
  - Low-impact: Bike intervals 6 x 1 min hard / 1 min easy, Rowing 8 x 30 s sprints / 60 s easy, or circuit of sled pushes, prowler (light-moderate), kettlebell swings (moderate and controlled hip hinge without flexion), farmer carries.
- Avoid heavy repeated loaded spinal flexion (no heavy kettlebell swings if they produce lumbar flexion under load; use lighter KB with perfect hip hinge form).

Core progression suggestions
- Emphasize anti-extension and anti-rotation: Pallof presses, dead-bug, suitcase/farmer carries, front planks, rolling ab wheel progressions only if technique is perfect, side planks, bird-dog.
- Avoid repeated weighted spinal flexion (no heavy sets of sit-ups/crunches with load).
- Daily 5–10 minute morning routine for desk worker: diaphragmatic breathing 2 min, 2 x 10 bird-dogs, 30–60 s plank, thoracic mobilization.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Encourage regular breaks from sitting: every 30–45 min stand, 1–2 min mobility or walking.
- Sleep: aim for 7–8 hours/night.
- Hydration and protein: target ~1.6–1.8 g/kg/day protein for strength gains (adjust by preferences/medical factors).
- Calorie guidance: if goal is general strength and body composition maintenance, aim for slight caloric surplus (~+200–300 kcal/day) to support strength gains; if fat loss desired, modest deficit. Adjust based on body composition goals.
- Anti-inflammatory lifestyle: prioritize whole foods, omega-3s, limit processed sugars; use icing or analgesics only per clinician if acute flare occurs.
- Recovery modalities: foam rolling, gentle yoga/stretching for thoracic and hip mobility 2–3x/week. Massage/soft tissue as needed.

Red flags and when to stop
- Any new or re-emerging radicular pain, numbness, progressive weakness — stop training and refer to physio/GP immediately.
- Sharp lumbar pain that reproduces symptoms; sudden severe pain during any lift — stop.

Example week (Week 6 sample)
Monday (Session A)
- Warm-up 10 min row + mobility
- Safety-bar or goblet squat: 4 x 6–8
- Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: 4 x 6–8
- Chest-supported row 3 x 8
- Reverse lunges 3 x 8 each
- Pallof press 3 x 10 each side
- Plank 3 x 45 s

Wednesday (Session B)
- Warm-up
- Trap-bar deadlift: 3 x 5 (moderate)
- Incline DB press: 4 x 6–8
- Single-arm DB row 3 x 8 each
- Hip thrust 3 x 8
- Farmer carry 3 x 40 m
- Dead-bug 3 x 10 each

Friday (Session C)
- Warm-up
- Bulgarian split squat 4 x 6 each
- Seated leg press 3 x 10
- Seated DB overhead press 3 x 8
- Cable chops (anti-rotation) 3 x 8 each side
- Bird-dog 3 x 8 each
- Thoracic mobility

Notes for the trainer
- Individualize loads, tempo, and exercise choices based on his exact movement quality and any remaining mobility restrictions.
- If client tolerates, you can introduce a safety-bar squat (safer spinal loading distribution) rather than goblet on later weeks.
- Use machines and chest-supported implements to load musculature without stressing the spine when appropriate.
- Communicate regularly with his physio if you plan to introduce higher loads or more demanding core drills.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into a printable week-by-week schedule with exact weights progression templates (percent-based or RPE).
- Provide demonstration cues for key lifts and core drills tailored to avoid lumbar flexion.
- Make a 4-week microcycle you can follow immediately, with specific warm-up sets and tempo.
